Question ID: CW_U06_L06_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

An author presentation begins with a short story excerpt. Which opening best prepares the audience?

answer.text: A. I am reading something I wrote, and that is all you need to know.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The audience needs title, genre, and a useful frame.

answer.text: B. My piece is a short story called The Last Bus. Listen for the short sentences because they show panic.

feedback.text: Correct. This gives title, genre, brief context, and a listening focus.

answer.text: C. This is long, so I will explain every event before reading.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Too much summary can overwhelm the presentation.

answer.text: D. I picked this because it is my favorite.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Personal preference alone does not prepare the audience.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which excerpt choice is strongest for an author presentation?

answer.text: A. A short section that clearly shows a craft choice and can be understood with brief context.

feedback.text: Correct. A focused excerpt helps the audience notice the writer's craft.

answer.text: B. The longest section, even if it needs ten minutes of explanation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Long excerpts can make the presentation unfocused.

answer.text: C. A random middle section with no context.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The audience needs a clear entry point.

answer.text: D. The first page only because first pages are always best.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The best excerpt depends on the presentation purpose.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which statement is craft reasoning rather than plot summary?

answer.text: A. The character goes outside, then comes back inside.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This only tells what happens. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. The poem is about rain.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This summarizes topic but does not explain craft.

answer.text: C. I used short fragments during the argument so the pacing feels tense and interrupted.

feedback.text: Correct. This names a craft choice and explains reader effect.

answer.text: D. The story has three characters.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This identifies content but not writer choice or effect.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

A student plans to read an excerpt but has no listening focus. What should the student add?

answer.text: A. A complete summary of every previous draft.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The audience needs focus, not a full drafting history.

answer.text: B. A warning that the presentation may be confusing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Planning should reduce confusion. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. A list of unrelated favorite books.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not support the selected work.

answer.text: D. A brief statement telling the audience what craft choice to notice.

feedback.text: Correct. A listening focus guides the audience toward the presentation purpose.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_L06_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which reflection best connects revision to growth?

answer.text: A. I changed it because I had to.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain the revision or growth.

answer.text: B. I replaced direct explanation with dialogue so readers can infer the character's fear.

feedback.text: Correct. This names the revision and explains the reader effect.

answer.text: C. I like the final version better.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a preference, not a craft explanation.

answer.text: D. I do not remember what changed.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A presentation should include clear process reflection.
